report:
Contrary to your expectation, clinical evidence demonstrates that **honey does help relieve acute cough in children aged 1 year and older**, though it is unsafe for infants under 12 months.

### Summary of Evidence

* **Proven Efficacy (Ages 1+):** Systematic reviews, including Cochrane Reviews and updated meta-analyses, show that a small dose of honey (2 to 5 mL) reduces cough frequency and severity more effectively than placebo or no treatment. It performs as well as or better than common over-the-counter cough suppressants like diphenhydramine or dextromethorphan for nighttime respiratory symptoms.
* **Medical Recommendations:** Guidelines from organizations such as the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) advise using honey as a low-cost, effective remedy to soothe irritated airways and thin mucus in children over 1 year.

### Critical Safety Exception

* **Contraindicated Under 1 Year:** Honey **must never** be given to infants under 12 months old. Honey can contain *Clostridium botulinum* spores, which can grow in an infant's immature digestive system and cause infant botulism—a rare but severe and potentially life-threatening illness.

### Conclusion

For children older than 1 year, clinical evidence supports using honey to ease acute cough symptoms. For infants under 1 year, honey should be strictly avoided due to botulism risk.

### Sources

* Cochrane Library: https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD007094.pub5/full
* PMC Systematic Review: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10570220/
* American Academy of Pediatrics (HealthyChildren.org): https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/chest-lungs/Pages/Coughs-and-Colds-Medicines-or-Home-Remedies.aspx
* Poison Control: https://www.poison.org/articles/dont-feed-honey-to-infants
